newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Zaveryukha sees quota on white sugar imports.
newsitem.headline: Zaveryukha sees quota on white sugar imports.

text.p: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Zaveryukha was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying on Monday that the cabinet had proposed imposing quotas on refined sugar imports.
He was quoted as saying that the cabinet also proposed a number of other measures aimed at supporting domestic agricultural producers, but he did not elaborate.
The Foreign Trade Ministry last year sent an order to the government calling for white sugar imports to be limited to 1.50 million tonnes, including 1.15 million from Ukraine.
But the government has so far failed to act on the order, casting doubts over whether it would support the plan to protect Russia's sugar refineries.
Domestic plants want to process raw sugar from Cuba rather than face Ukrainian and European competition.
Zaveryukha said domestic sugar prices fell 14.7 percent in 1996 over 1995 levels due to strong supplies.
